findings.note: Dead assertion: the warning check uses `&&` where `||` is meant. `if !strings.HasPrefix(w, "WORKFLOW_WARNING") && !strings.Contains(w, "loop_without_clean_exit")` can only fail when BOTH are false, so once the prefix matches the reason substring is never verified. The machine could propagate any WORKFLOW_WARNING body and this test would still pass; the reason text is only asserted in internal/fsm/workflow/workflow_test.go:355, not in the propagation path this test covers.

Global fixture leak: MaxDiffBytes (a package-level var in types.go) is set to 2 and restored four lines later by plain assignment, not defer. The t.Fatalf on the intervening truncation assertion aborts the goroutine before the restore, leaving MaxDiffBytes = 2 for every subsequent test in the package and cascading unrelated failures that hide the real one. Use defer func(old int){ MaxDiffBytes = old }(MaxDiffBytes).

evidence.note: restore is unreachable if the assertion between them fatals

findings.note: Fixture double-rename: sdlcWith already rewrites `workflow: sdlc-loop` to `workflow: sdlc-loop-test`, and the following line pipes the result through renamed(), whose Replace matches the `workflow: sdlc-loop` prefix again and yields `workflow: sdlc-loop-test-test`. Verified by direct experiment. Harmless today (only uniqueness matters) but it means the fixture name is not what the code reads, and the same pattern is repeated for ce.yaml.

findings.note: Hidden ordering coupling in TestM1InitErrors: the table shares one harness and cases mutate it cumulatively, and the assertion after the loop (mock id == "scen/ok#" + 16 a's) silently depends on the prep closure of the mock-registry-mismatch table row having seeded h.mockHash["/repo/scen/ok"]. Reordering or deleting that row breaks an assertion 30 lines away with no indication why. The cases are also not t.Run subtests, so a shared-state failure is not isolated.

evidence.note: prep seeds h.mockHash consumed far outside the loop
post-loop assertion depends on that earlier row

findings.note: Unguarded slice indexing in assertions: r.Untrusted[0], r.Warnings[0] and Snapshot.Warnings[0] are indexed without a length check, so a regression that produces an empty slice panics and aborts the whole test binary instead of reporting a clean failure for the one case. Cheap fix: len(...) == 0 || ... in the same condition, as is already done for r.NeedsInput == nil at line 226.

findings.note: renamed(body any) takes an untyped parameter and its type switch has no default: any value that is neither string nor []byte silently produces empty workflow bytes, turning a future call-site mistake into a confusing ERR_WORKFLOW_INVALID rather than a compile error. A []byte parameter with an explicit string(...) at the two string call sites would be type-safe.

evidence.note: type switch over any with no default branch
